children: Several prominent developers are urging core developers to halt the Ethereum Glamsterdam upgrade in its current form. They warn that its planned gas changes could break smart contracts that hold user funds.
“Please don’t break the chain,” wrote the founder of Curve Finance. “It looks like the Glamsterdam upgrade would lead to another emergency hard fork back, with a lot of drama.”
Developers Push Back on Ethereum Glamsterdam Gas Plan
At the center of the dispute is EIP-8037, which raises gas costs for creating new state, such as storage entries and new contracts.
However, some smart contracts set a fixed gas amount for these steps or check the remaining gas during a transaction.
Once prices rise, those calls could run out of gas and fail. Because deployed contracts are immutable, developers cannot simply patch them, which could leave user funds stuck.
A prominent DeFi developer called the plan “completely ridiculous.”
Another developer said his team had found the same issues a security firm later flagged, even before Glamsterdam went live on the Sepolia testnet.
“Rushing out Glamsterdam now disregarding the community feedback would be a mistake,” the developer wrote.
also opposed the upgrade. “I’m not gonna push for a fork that breaks invariants that were unknown until ~2 weeks ago,” the security researcher wrote.

Ethereum Advocate Reverses Call for Fast Activation

The pushback even changed minds among Ethereum Glamsterdam supporters. An influential Ethereum community member first called for activation “asap.” In his view, Ethereum guarantees access to the network, not specific gas prices.

Hours later, however, the advocate reversed course. “We should (clearly, now) not continue towards Glam activation asap. I was wrong to say so,” he wrote. The problem, he added, is “essentially worse than is generally understood.”

The advocate also admitted that the community collectively failed on the design, due diligence, and public communication. Gas introspection, he wrote, is “a very serious issue that needs immediate remediation and way more sunlight.”
As a result, core developers face pressure to publish more data before Ethereum Glamsterdam reaches mainnet. The dispute also lands as Ethereum ETFs log their worst month for flows since launch.
Meanwhile, Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has already called the next upgrade, Hegota, Ethereum’s last “normal” fork.

title: Ethereum Glamsterdam Upgrade Could Break the Chain, Developers Warn
